boundary_rationale: Onset: the book opens on two datelines in two counting systems - בִּשְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.1.1, a regnal/exilic year the book never names an era for) and הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַחֲמִישִׁ֔ית לְגָל֖וּת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ יוֹיָכִֽין (oshb:Ezek.1.2, the fifth year of Jehoiachin's exile) - followed at oshb:Ezek.1.3 by the superscription הָיֹ֣ה הָיָ֣ה דְבַר יְ֠הוָה אֶל יְחֶזְקֵ֨אל, an infinitive-absolute-plus-perfect word-event with a THIRD-PERSON addressee ('to Ezekiel', not 'to me'). This verb and addressee shape are why the verse sits in the 49-verse any-form word-event count and not the 48-verse first-person family (sweep: verses containing the word-event phrase in any form, 49; the 48 excludes this one verse by predicate). It is weighed here as a real onset in its own right, not folded into or discounted against the vision that follows. The same verse also carries וַתְּהִ֥י עָלָ֛יו שָׁ֖ם יַד יְהוָֽה, the hand-of-YHWH construct that opens the book's first vision (one of 7 verses carrying the construct). Close: the scene runs unbroken to oshb:Ezek.1.28, מַרְאֵ֖ה דְּמ֣וּת כְּבוֹד יְהוָ֑ה וָֽאֶרְאֶה֙ וָאֶפֹּ֣ל עַל פָּנַ֔י וָאֶשְׁמַ֖ע ק֥וֹל מְדַבֵּֽר, glossed by the WEB as “This was the appearance of the likeness of Yahweh’s glory. When I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard a voice of one that spoke” (web:Ezek.1.28). No word-event, messenger, recognition or utterance formula interrupts 1:4-1:27 (the transport-verb and 'he said to me' sweeps that mark scene changes elsewhere in the book's visions do not begin until chapter 8), so the throne-theophany carries no formula-marked internal seam; the samekh recorded after 1:28 and the fresh 'he said to me' that opens oshb:Ezek.2.1 together mark the vision/commission seam on the FAR side of this unit; the onset evidence at oshb:Ezek.2.1 is weighed there.

strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating oshb:Ezek.1.1-1.3 as its own superscription unit, separate from the vision it introduces. Rejected because the vision proper (1:4-1:28) carries no independent onset device of its own - it simply continues the sentence the hand-of-YHWH clause opens - so cutting after 1:3 would manufacture a seam the bytes do not mark, and would still leave a 25-verse remainder with the same cap problem.
device_notes: Whole-chapter span (28 verses), well above the 7-10 typical density and above the 14-16 stretch cap for measured/listed blocks even though this is not such a block; disclosed and held at low confidence rather than forced into an unsupported internal cut. MT 1:3 is cited only under the 49-verse any-form word-event count, never blended with the 48-verse first-person family. K/Q at 1:8 checked before quoting: the unit does not splice the disputed word. The OSHB editorial note at 1:11 is disclosed as single-witness apparatus, not a reading change. Paseq at 1:1 and 1:27 disclosed count-only (single-witness); no intra-verse position is claimed.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:4 לֶךְ בֹּא֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Ezek.3.4) ('go, get you to the house of Israel'), a fresh 'he said to me' turning from the scroll itself to the audience it will be spoken to; 3:7 characterizes them, כִּ֚י כָּל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל חִזְקֵי מֵ֥צַח וּקְשֵׁי לֵ֖ב הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.3.7) ('for all the house of Israel are obstinate and hard-hearted'). A pe is recorded after 3:9, כְּשָׁמִ֛יר חָזָ֥ק מִצֹּ֖ר נָתַ֣תִּי מִצְחֶ֑ךָ ('I have made your forehead as a diamond'), closing with a further rebellious-house refrain, כִּ֛י בֵּֽית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.3.9) (the third of six). That mark is disclosed but not read as the unit's own close: 3:10 reopens with 'moreover he said to me' on the same audience-description topic, and cutting there would leave 3:10-3:11 (2 verses, no word-event of its own) detached from the speech they continue. Close: 3:11, אִֽם יִשְׁמְע֖וּ וְאִם יֶחְדָּֽלוּ (oshb:Ezek.3.11) ('whether they will hear, or whether they will refuse'), immediately before the return-transport of 3:12 begins a distinct, vision-texture scene.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Ezek.3.6 (paseq, single-witness, count-only)
oshb:Ezek.3.9 (pe follows, single-witness, mid-unit, disclosed and not cut)
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting after the pe at 3:9. Rejected because the two verses that would remain, 3:10-3:11, share the same 'he said to me' commissioning texture as 3:4-3:9 with no onset device distinguishing them, and they would stand as a two-verse unit whose opening is a further 'he said to me' in the same speech, with no word-event, hand-of-YHWH construct or dateline of its own (sweep: 0 of the 49 any-form word-event verses, 0 of the 7 hand-of-YHWH verses and 0 of the 14 dateline verses fall in 3:10-3:11).
device_notes: Paseq at 3:6 disclosed count-only (single-witness); no intra-verse position claimed. The pe following 3:9 is disclosed as single-witness sub-paragraph evidence inside the unit, weighed and not adopted as the cut point for the reason given in boundary_rationale. A pe follows MT 3:3 (single witness), the paragraph mark standing just behind this unit's opening verse.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:16 carries the book's first strict word-event formula, וַיְהִ֕י מִקְצֵ֖ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.3.16) ('at the end of seven days, Yahweh's word came to me, saying'), a hard seam, since a strict word-event opens a new oracle and no unit runs across one (3:16 is one of the 39 strict-form verses and one of the 48 in the first-person family). A pe is recorded after this verse; the inventory does not carry intra-verse position, so no claim is made about whether the mark falls before or after 3:17's watchman charge, צֹפֶ֥ה נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.3.17) ('I have made you a watchman to the house of Israel'). A samekh follows 3:19, between the wicked-man case (3:18-19) and the righteous-man case (3:20-21); disclosed as an internal paragraph mark, not a unit cut, since both cases are one paired illustration of the same watchman charge and no fresh onset device stands at 3:20. Close: 3:21, at the second samekh, before the hand-of-YHWH reopens the scene at 3:22.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Ezek.3.16 (word-event, strict form, hard seam onset; pe follows, single-witness)
oshb:Ezek.3.19 (samekh follows, single-witness, mid-unit, disclosed and not cut)
oshb:Ezek.3.20 (OSHB editorial note, single-witness: a ketiv/qere read with L against BHS)
oshb:Ezek.3.21 (samekh follows, single-witness, unit-final)
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit backward to include 3:12-3:15, uniting the return-journey and the watchman charge under one 'onset at 3:12' reading. Rejected because 3:16 supplies its own strict word-event, a hard seam no unit may cross, independent of how short either side then runs.
device_notes: The editorial note at 3:20 is disclosed as single-witness apparatus (an accepted ketiv/qere divergence from BHS agreeing with L); no reading is asserted beyond what the note itself states. Samekh at 3:19 disclosed as mid-unit texture; samekh at 3:21 is the unit's close mark. Neither parashah mark is read as deciding the boundary by itself.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:22 וַתְּהִ֥י עָלַ֛י שָׁ֖ם יַד יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.3.22) ('Yahweh's hand was there on me'), the hand-of-YHWH construct read here as a genuine vision onset (contrast oshb:Ezek.3.14, where the construct accompanies the spirit carrying the prophet away, a transit rather than a new scene) because it opens a fresh scene: 'arise, go out into the plain'. 3:25 announces that עֲבוֹתִ֔ים (oshb:Ezek.3.25) ('ropes') will be put on the prophet; the word recurs at 4:8 in the siege sign-act, across the 3:27/4:1 seam (accent_stripped tier: the same consonants and vowels under a different accent), so the muteness command and the sign-acts share a device, and that continuity is weighed here against the seam even though the unit boundary stands. 3:26 carries the fifth rebellious-house refrain, כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה. Close: 3:27, הַשֹּׁמֵ֤עַ יִשְׁמָע֙ וְהֶחָדֵ֣ל יֶחְדָּ֔ל כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.3.27) ('he who hears, let him hear; and he who refuses, let him refuse; for they are a rebellious house') - the sixth verse in chapters 2-3 to name the rebellious house (sweep: 12 verses book-wide name it, six of them in chapters 2-3), and the parent P1's close; a samekh is recorded after this verse. Across the seam, 4:1 opens with וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ (oshb:Ezek.4.1) ('and you, son of man'), spliced at byte tier as the 3:27 clause is, and turns to the command to take a tile, the sub-onset that starts the sign-acts. The unit therefore stops at 3:27 and does not extend into 4:1; the seam's near side is closed by the refrain and the samekh after 3:27 (single witness), and its far side is opened by that sub-onset.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Ezek.3.22 (hand-of-YHWH, vision onset, hard seam)
oshb:Ezek.3.25 (continuity device עבותים 'ropes', disclosed against 4:8 across the parent seam)
oshb:Ezek.3.27 (rebellious-house refrain, 6th of 12 verses book-wide; paseq recorded twice at this verse, single-witness, count-only; samekh follows, single-witness, P1-final)
strongest_rejected_alternative: Placing the P1/P2 parent seam at 3:15/3:16 instead of 3:27/4:1, on the strength of 3:16's own strict word-event and the seven-day close it answers. Weighed on the bytes, the onset side of that seam is strong: 3:16 sets מִקְצֵ֖ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.3.16) ('at the end of seven days') before its strict word-event, and a pe follows 3:16 itself (single witness), after the word-event verse rather than before it. Its close side is narrative: 3:15 ends the journey to the exiles on seven days of sitting among them, a report rather than a refrain. The rebellious-house refrain runs on both sides of 3:16 (sweep: of the six verses in chapters 2-3 that name the rebellious house, four stand before 3:16 and two after it), so a parent seam there would divide that series, whereas at 3:27/4:1 the series' sixth verse stands on the close side and the sub-onset of 4:1 on the onset side. The alternative is kept as a held question and not argued away, because the ropes of 3:25, taken up at 4:8, tie the muteness command (3:22-27) to the sign-acts (4:1-17) across the later seam.
device_notes: Operative-category deviation disclosed: this span also carries commission_narrative texture (the muteness charge proper runs 3:24-3:27 inside this vision-opened scene); labelled vision_report because the unit's onset device is the hand-of-YHWH construct at 3:22. Paseq at 3:27 occurs twice (double occurrence on one verse), disclosed count-only, single-witness. The ropes word shared by 3:25 and 4:8 is disclosed as continuity across the 3:27/4:1 seam; it argues for the closeness of the two units, while the refrain close at 3:27 and the sub-onset at 4:1 keep the seam between them. The witness records a samekh after MT 3:21 (single witness), the mark this unit's onset can claim from its own side.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 6:11 opens with a fresh messenger formula; the pe-marked recognition close that precedes it stands at oshb:Ezek.6.10 - כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה הַכֵּ֨ה בְכַפְּךָ֜ (oshb:Ezek.6.11) ('thus says the Lord Yahweh: strike with your hand') - a gesture command distinct in address from 6:1-10's oracle to the mountains. Close: 6:14, וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.6.14) ('then they shall know that I am Yahweh'), the strict recognition formula, before 7:1 reopens with its own word-event.

strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging 6:11-14 into 6:1-10 as one long mountains-oracle. Rejected because a close and an onset meet here. Behind the seam, 6:10 ends on the recognition formula and a pe follows it (single witness); ahead of it, 6:11 opens on a fresh messenger formula that turns from the oracle to the mountains of Israel to a gesture command for the prophet. The resulting unit is short, but both of its edges are marked.

device_notes: Four-verse unit; justified by the pe-marked close behind it and the fresh messenger-formula onset in front of it, not by size. Paseq at 6:13 disclosed count-only, single-witness.
